title: Prognostic indices of inflammatory markers, cognitive function and fatigue for survival in patients with localised colorectal cancer
notes: Longitudinal cohort with healthy controls; median follow-up 91.2 months. Survival analysis (Cox regression) testing whether inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), cognitive function, and fatigue predict OS and DFS. ALL cytokine associations with survival were NULL: IL-6 log HR 0.99 (0.82-1.19, p=0.88), TNF-α log HR 0.96 (0.81-1.15, p=0.68). Cognitive impairment did NOT predict OS or DFS. Fatigue did NOT predict OS or DFS. Only baseline clinical variables (stage, CEA, diabetes, lymphovascular invasion) predicted survival. Population-level data: 44% of CRC patients had cognitive impairment vs 15% healthy controls; 52% had fatigue vs 26% controls. Cytokine levels elevated in CRC patients at baseline normalized post-chemotherapy.
extraction_status: META_ONLY — survival/prognostic study with ALL NULL results for cytokine/cognition/fatigue → survival; no inflammation→cognition edge evidence; useful only for population prevalence data
null_findings: ALL cytokine, cognition, fatigue predictors NULL for both OS and DFS
